title: Speed up GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators (cache response, fetch concurrently)
description: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators re-runs the entire Triple Screen pipeline once per daily bar in the requested range, and fetches daily then weekly OHLCV sequentially. This task covers the two lowest-risk, highest-leverage fixes from docs/ideas.md's performance entry: caching the computed IndicatorHistoryResponse itself (a pure function of daily/weekly OHLCV 'as of today', so a (ticker, range)-keyed same-day-TTL cache makes every request after the first same-day one instant) and fetching daily+weekly OHLCV concurrently instead of sequentially. Explicitly excludes the bigger, riskier 'vectorize the per-bar loop' rewrite and the 'downsample very long ranges' idea (both flagged in docs/ideas.md as needing their own separate scoping) -- those are not in scope here.

checklist.step: Add a (ticker, range)-keyed cache for the computed IndicatorHistoryResponse with a same-day TTL, analogous to the existing ohlcv_cache/extended_data_cache tables.
Fetch daily and weekly OHLCV concurrently in get_indicator_history instead of sequentially.

Decide and record whether the existing 24h OHLCV cache TTL should also change now that daily bars only close once per trading day (docs/ideas.md's TTL question) -- record a decisions entry either way, even if the decision is to leave it unchanged.
Unit tests covering cache hit, cache miss, and TTL expiry for the new response cache, plus a test that the concurrent fetch still degrades correctly if one of the two calls fails.
Confirm no response shape change (this is caching-only) -- if it turns out one is needed, regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types.
